- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong upward bias; apply downward correction of 3–8% for the first 5–7 days of forecast.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and continue rising; cap forecast slope after peak or introduce early mean-reversion decay.
- True outcomes often show mean reversion toward mid-range values after initial volatility; model fails to reflect this; apply smoothing or decay factor to forecast tail (last 5–7 days).
- If true outcome shows sustained high values (e.g., >85) after a low, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or introduce downward bias for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Sentiment history is irrelevant in these examples (all 0.00), so no sentiment-based correction rules are triggered — but if sentiment becomes non-zero, model should adjust forecast directionality based on sentiment polarity.
